items.note: This is あります in the sense "take place": the place takes で, not に. Contrast ちかくにえきがあります (Lesson 12), where あります means "exist" and the place takes に.

items.note: This から means "because, so" — a different job from the から you already know for "from" (Lesson 3's なんじからなんじまで, Lesson 6's アメリカからきました). It attaches to the end of the reason clause: clause1から、clause2, as in いいてんきですから、こうえんでひるごはんをたべませんか, "The weather is nice, so shall we have lunch in the park?"

items.note: Used after [noun]は to soften a refusal without a direct 'no' — e.g. アニメは ちょっと…, 'Anime is not really my thing.' Often follows すみません or ざんねんですが.

items.note: みます → みましょう. The chapter drills all four verbs (いく・みる・する・あう) across ます / ませんか / ましょう; this is the cell for みる.

items.note: ましょう assumes agreement and moves straight to action — more decisive than いきませんか above, which politely asks first before assuming a yes.

items.english: There is a festival in Asakusa on Saturday.
items.target: どようびにあさくさでおまつリがあります
items.pronunciation: doyōbi ni Asakusa de omatsuri ga arimasu
items.note: Demonstrates place + で + event + が + あります, 'an event takes place somewhere' (GRAMMAR 1).

items.english: Shall we see a movie together on the weekend?
items.target: しゅうまつにいっしょにえいがをみませんか
items.pronunciation: shūmatsu ni issho ni eiga o mimasen ka
items.note: Demonstrates verb[ます-stem]+ませんか, used to invite someone to do something (GRAMMAR 2).

items.note: Demonstrates verb[ます-stem]+ましょう, used when inviting the listener to do something together (GRAMMAR 3).

items.english: The weather is nice, so shall we have lunch in the park?
items.target: いいてんきですから、こうえんでひるごはんをたべませんか
items.pronunciation: ii tenki desu kara, kōen de hirugohan o tabemasen ka
items.note: Demonstrates clause1から、clause2 (reason) combined with an invitation (GRAMMAR 4).
はい can replace ええ for a slightly more formal 'yes'.
items.reviewNote: Source shows alternatives 'ええ／はい、 ぜひ。'; ええ kept as the primary form, はい noted as an alternate opener.

items.english: I'm sorry, but anime is not really my thing.
items.target: すみません。アニメはちょっと
items.reviewNote: Source GRAMMAR table gives the pattern 'すみません。 noun は ちょっと…。'; filled with アニメ (anime), reusing this chapter's dialogue topic. The trailing ellipsis was resolved into a closed sentence since a placeholder can't be spoken.

items.english: Unfortunately, Saturday doesn't really work for me.
items.target: ざんねんですが、どようびはちょっと
items.pronunciation: zannen desu ga, doyōbi wa chotto
items.note: ざんねんですが (unfortunately) softens the refusal more than すみません — used especially for a scheduling conflict rather than a taste mismatch.
items.reviewNote: Source GRAMMAR table gives the pattern 'ざんねんですが、 noun は ちょっと…。'; filled with どようび (Saturday) for variety from the previous card. The trailing ellipsis was resolved into a closed sentence.

items.note: ゆき (snow) + まつり (festival, as in おまつり from Key Sentence 1) = ゆきまつり (snow festival).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form にしぐち, 'west exit'.
にし (west) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = にしぐち (west exit).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form ひがしぐち, 'east exit'.
ひがし (east) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = ひがしぐち (east exit).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form きたぐち, 'north exit'.
きた (north) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = きたぐち (north exit).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form みなみぐち, 'south exit'.
みなみ (south) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = みなみぐち (south exit).
すきました here comes from すきます, "become empty/hungry" — a different word from すき, "like, favorite" (Lesson 15), despite the similar sound. おなかがすきました literally means "my stomach has become empty."

items.note: なにか (something) is used in questions and positive statements, e.g. なにかのみませんか; contrast なにも (Lesson 8), which only ever pairs with a negative verb to mean "nothing."
A more neutral, slightly formal synonym of ちょっと (Lesson 10) — both mean "a bit, a little," but ちょっと is the everyday casual choice.
Verb form of やすみ (Lesson 3, "break, day off") — やすみます is the action "to rest," while やすみ names the break itself.

items.english: There's a fireworks festival in Yokohama on Sunday. Shall we go together?
items.target: にちようびによこはまではなびたいかいがあります。いっしょにいきませんか
items.pronunciation: nichiyōbi ni Yokohama de hanabi taikai ga arimasu. issho ni ikimasen ka

items.english: What time does the fireworks festival start?
items.target: はなびたいかいはなんじからですか
items.pronunciation: hanabi taikai wa nanji kara desu ka
items.scene: asking what time an event starts

items.english: It starts at 7:00. Let's meet at 6:00 at the west exit of Yokohama Station.
items.target: 7じからです。6じによこはまえきのにしぐちであいましょう
items.ttsText: しちじからです。ろくじによこはまえきのにしぐちであいましょう
items.pronunciation: shichi-ji kara desu. roku-ji ni Yokohama-eki no nishiguchi de aimashō
items.scene: arranging where to meet before an event

items.english: 6:00 at the west exit of Yokohama Station, right? Got it.
items.target: 6じによこはまえきのにしぐちですね。わかりました
items.ttsText: ろくじによこはまえきのにしぐちですね。わかりました
items.pronunciation: roku-ji ni Yokohama-eki no nishiguchi desu ne. wakarimashita
items.scene: confirming a meeting time and place
items.note: わかりました (wakarimashita) means 'understood, got it' — used to confirm you've understood a plan or instruction.

items.english: Smith-san, I am having a party at my home on Sunday, the 15th. Would you like to come?
items.target: スミスさん、15にちのにちようびにうちでパーティーをします。きませんか
items.ttsText: スミスさん、じゅうごにちのにちようびにうちでパーティーをします。きませんか
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san, jūgo-nichi no nichiyōbi ni uchi de pātī o shimasu. kimasen ka
items.scene: inviting someone to a party at one's own home
items.note: きませんか (not いきませんか) is used specifically when inviting someone to your own home or an event you yourself are hosting.
items.reviewNote: Chapter's only sentence demonstrating きませんか used for an invitation to the speaker's own home/event, a nuance highlighted in this chapter's NOTES; extracted from the SPEAKING PRACTICE dialogue under the function-word exception since the pattern appears nowhere else in the chapter.

items.target: ありがとうございます。ぜひ
items.scene: accepting an invitation to someone's home or a planned event
items.note: Contrasts with ええ、ぜひ or いいですね。ぜひ — ありがとうございます。ぜひ is used specifically when accepting an invitation to the speaker's home, a planned event, or something already decided.
items.reviewNote: Chapter's only sentence demonstrating this accepting-register nuance, highlighted in this chapter's NOTES; extracted from the SPEAKING PRACTICE dialogue under the function-word exception.

items.english: You're thirsty, aren't you? Shall we drink something?
items.target: のどがかわきましたね。なにかのみませんか
items.pronunciation: nodo ga kawakimashita ne. nanika nomimasen ka
items.note: なにか (something) plus ませんか invites without naming the drink.

items.scene: answering an invitation to drink something because you're thirsty

items.english: You're tired, aren't you? Shall we rest a bit?
items.target: つかれましたね。すこしやすみませんか
items.note: すこし (a bit) softens the suggestion to rest.
